solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Political message from an unpleasant person needing support

parts.note: the indefinite article gives the single letter A
a git is British slang for a contemptible or unpleasant person
a prop is something that holds another thing up

explanation.surface: A political communication comes from some nasty character who needs backing.
explanation.walkthrough: GIT is everyday British slang for a nasty or foolish person. 'needing' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitprop is propaganda, especially left-wing political material spread through art or literature.

clue.text: Sail for port

explanation.surface: A sailor sets off by sailing to a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A genoa is a large jib sail on a yacht, and Genoa is the major Italian seaport city.

clue.text: May be mum and dad once showing 10

definitions.text: May be mum and dad once
definitions.meaning: read as two words, this describes a mother or father who has since changed gender, having been one parent before
10 across is clarity, so this means clear or see-through

explanation.surface: Someone who may once have been a mother and a father displays great lucidity.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as TRANS PARENT for the first reading; the cross-reference to 10 (LUCIDITY) supplies the plain sense of being clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Something transparent shows clarity, letting light or meaning through plainly; the split reading suggests a parent who has transitioned.

clue.text: Engine cooler but house warmer

explanation.surface: A device that cools a motor yet heats a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's radiator dissipates engine heat, while a domestic radiator heats rooms, so one word covers both appliances.

clue.text: The endlessly ridiculous pun can be beautiful

indicators.note: the letters can be turned into something else, signalling a rearrangement of the fodder
without its end, the word The loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A really silly pun can still be lovely, if you drop the end of the article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims The to TH; 'can be' tells you to rearrange TH with RIDICULOUS and PUN, fifteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulchritudinous is a grand, rarely used adjective for physically lovely or attractive.

clue.text: Epitomise the origins of every mischievous boy or deviant youth

indicators.note: the origin of each word is where it starts, so take the initial letter of each of the six words

explanation.surface: Typify the beginnings of every naughty lad or wayward teenager.
explanation.definitionFit: To embody something is to give it concrete form, being a perfect example of it.

clue.text: Minder in Tesco working to suppress the start of riot

indicators.note: suppress means holding down within, so one piece is kept inside the other
working suggests the letters being worked over into a new order
the start of a word is its first letter, here of riot

explanation.surface: A security guard in a supermarket branch works to put down an incipient disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges TESCO to ESCOT; 'to suppress' puts R, 'the start of riot', inside it. Tesco is a large British supermarket chain.
explanation.definitionFit: An escort is someone who accompanies and protects another, just as a minder guards a person.

clue.text: At the beginning, Boris somehow hoped to be promiscuous

indicators.note: at the beginning of the name Boris stands its first letter
somehow says the letters of hoped are set out in some other way

explanation.surface: From the start, Boris somehow hoped he could sleep around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the beginning' gives B from Boris; 'somehow' rearranges HOPED to EDHOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Bed-hopping means having many casual sexual partners in turn, which is promiscuity.

clue.text: Nice summer on court covered by joint investigator

indicators.note: covered by means wrapped inside, so the first pieces go within the other

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar or club, informally called a joint
été is French for summer, Nice being the French city

explanation.surface: A summer on a tennis court in the south of France ends at a sleazy bar, under the eye of a sleuth.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice is the French city here, not 'pleasant', so its summer is in French. 'covered by' puts the summer and court inside the joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A detective is a police officer or private agent who looks into crimes.

clue.text: Honorary penny given in international assistance

indicators.note: given in here means placed among, so one piece is inserted into the other

parts.note: UN, the United Nations, stands for international bodies
aid is help or assistance

explanation.surface: An unpaid honorary post brings a single coin in foreign aid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given in' sets the penny inside the international assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: An honorary role is held without salary, so it is done for no pay.

clue.text: Clarity of blue, essentially without a sharpness

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so take the central letters of blue
without says the word a is dropped from the sharpness word

parts.note: acidity is the sharp, sour quality of a taste

explanation.surface: The clarity of blue, in essence, lacks any edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes LU from the middle of blue; 'without' removes A from ACIDITY, leaving CIDITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucidity is clearness of thought or expression, the quality of being easily understood.

clue.text: Road features strange caste getting approval

indicators.note: strange suggests the word caste is set out oddly, in a fresh order

parts.note: yes is a word of assent or approval

explanation.surface: An unusual social group wins approval for features of the highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges the caste letters before the approval word. Cat's eyes are the reflective studs set into British roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Cat's eyes are reflective studs set in a road's surface to mark lanes at night.

clue.text: Intense dislike of the upper classes by short French men sans frontières

parts.note: A and B are the top social grades in the British classification of class

indicators.note: French for without borders, so each word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: The upper crust's loathing of Frenchmen, described in borderless French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sans frontières' strips the outer letters from short, French and men, giving HOR, RENC and E. AB comes from the British social grades A and B (upper and upper-middle class).
explanation.definitionFit: Abhorrence is a feeling of strong loathing or revulsion.

clue.text: Is leaving troubled Vietnam, senile from subjugation

indicators.note: troubled means stirred up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: Is read as the plural of the letter I, two of them

explanation.surface: Is someone departing a war-torn Vietnam, aged and frail, to escape oppression?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is leaving' removes the two I's from VIETNAM SENILE, and 'troubled' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Enslavement is the state of being held in bondage, the extreme of subjugation.

clue.text: Burger or a Chinese may be? Simple last dish

parts.note: a Big Mac is a famous burger, so mac stands for one

indicators.note: may be suggests these letters could become something else when rearranged
the last letter of the word Simple

explanation.surface: Is a fast-food burger or a Chinese takeaway the plain final course?
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges OR A CHINESE with E ('Simple last') to ARONI CHEESE.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroni cheese is a baked pasta meal of macaroni in a cheese sauce.

clue.text: This vegetable is at home in French lodge

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: an auberge is a French inn
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: This vegetable feels right at home in a French inn.
explanation.walkthrough: IN = at home is a common convention.
explanation.definitionFit: The aubergine, also called eggplant, is a purple-skinned fruit cooked as a vegetable.

clue.text: Appropriate action needs a belief, oddly

parts.note: a suit is a legal action in court

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth, of belief

explanation.surface: A fitting lawsuit requires faith, strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: SUIT is a legal action (lawsuit); 'oddly' picks B, L, E from belief.
explanation.definitionFit: Suitable means fitting or right for the purpose.

clue.text: Better music arrangement without piquancy from Red Hot Chili Peppers?

definitions.text: without piquancy from Red Hot Chili Peppers?

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it

indicators.note: an arrangement sets the word music out in a different order

explanation.surface: A rock fan claims to improve on a Red Hot Chili Peppers tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' rearranges MUSIC to SICUM. Take away the 'Red Hot' from chili peppers and what remains is the mild, sweet sort of pepper.
explanation.definitionFit: Capsicum is the sweet or bell pepper, the mild relative of the fiery chilli.

clue.text: See 16
Unexpectedly French and English articles and goods

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article
a is the English indefinite article
wares are goods for sale

explanation.surface: Suddenly, French and English grammar items and merchandise appear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' does duty for both languages: UN is a French article, A an English one.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken unawares means caught by surprise, without warning.

clue.text: Violent secret life uncovered when looking back

indicators.note: looking back says the letters are read from right to left
uncovered means stripping the cover, the outer letters, from secret and life

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a ferocious hidden past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' strips the outer letters of secret and life; 'when looking back' turns the result round.
explanation.definitionFit: Fierce means savage and aggressive, ready to attack.

clue.text: Tips obtainable from Eric, lead guitarist

indicators.note: obtainable from says the letters can be got by rearranging this fodder
the lead letter of Eric is its first

explanation.surface: A lead guitarist named Eric, perhaps Clapton, collects tips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' gives E from Eric; 'obtainable from' rearranges E + GUITARIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratuities are tips, extra money given for good service.

clue.text: See 11
Messenger's Großstadt

indicators.note: the 's stands for has, so the word Messenger holds the answer within it

explanation.surface: A courier's big city.
explanation.walkthrough: A Großstadt is the German term for a city of over 100,000 people.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is a large industrial city in Germany's Ruhr region.

clue.text: Success with other plan so far

parts.note: a hit is a success

indicators.note: to plan is to lay out or arrange, so the letters of other are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A winning plan with another scheme up to now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plan' rearranges OTHER to HERTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitherto means until now, up to this point in time.

clue.text: See 7
See 14
Public abuse of Pope Paul IV (and Leo II)

indicators.note: abuse means mistreating, so the letters are mangled into a new order
the Roman numeral four picks the fourth letter of Paul
the Roman numeral two picks the second letter of Leo

explanation.surface: Misuse of the pontiffs Paul IV and Leo II.
explanation.walkthrough: Popes' regnal numbers become letter positions: 'IV' takes L from Paul, 'II' takes E from Leo; 'abuse of' rearranges POPE + L + E.
explanation.definitionFit: The people means the general public, the populace as a whole.

clue.text: Permanent recording label's musical interval

indicators.note: the 's stands for has, so the permanent word has the label inside

parts.note: set in stone means permanent, so stone stands for it
EMI is a well-known British record label

explanation.surface: A lasting record company's musical step.
explanation.walkthrough: EMI set in STONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A semitone is a half step, the smallest interval in Western music.
